## Active contributors

People with a commit in the six months up to each month, and those of them who
have also contributed to a napari plugin's repo.

```{python}
#| renderings: [light, dark]
show(plots.active_contributors(data.active_contributors()))
```

## Contributors by release

Each bar is one napari release. Its width runs from the previous release to
this one, and its height is the release's contributors (everyone in the
release notes' author list) per month of that time, so the bar's area is the
people. Many people in a short cycle make a tall bar. *New* means not in any
earlier release's list. Patch releases out less than two weeks after the one
before are left out: a handful of people over a few days spikes the rate. The
last bar is the release in development.

How napari releases changed:

- 2025-09-05: napari adopts [EffVer](https://effver.org) (Intended Effort
  Versioning, [napari#8243](https://github.com/napari/napari/pull/8243)): the
  version bump says how much effort upgrading takes, not whether the release
  is "big".
- mid-2026: releases come about monthly, from 0.8.0 on.
- 2026-09-22: the
  [monthly release cadence](https://napari.org/dev/developers/core_team/release_policy.html)
  is official ([docs#1126](https://github.com/napari/docs/pull/1126)). These
  monthly cycles are the tallest bars, on the right.

```{python}
#| renderings: [light, dark]
show(plots.release_contributors(data.release_contributors()))
```
